relevance_note: Post-mortem metabolomic study of one identifiable person with SSADH deficiency: "a 37 y.o. male patient with succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency (SSADHD)".
method_note: Read by hand; output assembled with a short Python script from values chosen while reading, then every span checked verbatim. Single patient labelled 'patient' (rule 5); the 8 control autopsies in Table 1 are not in scope and get no rows. No ALDH5A1 variant or genotype is printed or tied to the patient anywhere in the paper, so the variants table is empty (no 'not reported' variant row, since the paper does not tie a variant to him). Patient was first reported by Haan et al. 1985 (ref [18]); described first-hand here, so source_reference_in_review is 'not reported'. Age 37 recorded as age at death and as age at last evaluation (post-mortem tissue). 'Seizures or epilepsy' is set observed from the stated cause of death 'SUDEP (sudden unexpected death of epilepsy)'; the paper gives no other epilepsy history. 'a clinical course typical of SSADHD' gives no specific features. Metabolite findings are from post-mortem tissue versus controls. Contradiction: Results say 'cre in liver was within the range of control', while Discussion says 'Significant elevations of GHB, 4-GBA, SSA, guanidinoacetic acid, creatine and homocarnosine were also detected in the liver and kidney of the patient'; brain creatine is reported decreased; the liver/kidney feature row omits creatine for this reason. The infectious-disease screen (negative) is recorded as four excluded rows. cohort_size_as_stated null (n = 4 controls are not patients).
